**Playbook for the fishery game**

- Compute the true sustainable per-boat catch before deciding: sustainable total harvest is 1/3 of the current stock (since regrowth is 50% of what's left, the steady-state leaves 2/3 intact). Divide by the number of boats.
- In early and middle seasons, submit exactly the sustainable share — no more. This worked: the stock only drifted from 100 to 92.5 over five seasons, and I banked steady catches throughout.
- Read the history to judge the other boats. If they're all near the sustainable share, match it exactly; cooperation held across all six seasons here, so don't preemptively defect out of fear.
- If others overshoot persistently and the stock is clearly declining, still don't panic-grab — but do take the full sustainable share rather than under-catching, since my restraint alone won't save the stock.
- Only in the final season is conservation worthless: there is no future, so take far more than the sustainable share. Grab aggressively — 20 worked well and cost nothing.
- In the final season, consider grabbing even harder next time — the stock was still ~92 with three boats, so the ceiling is roughly a third of the stock each if we split it evenly. A bid in the 25–30 range is worth testing; rivals may also defect, so some of my grab may go unmet, but there's no downside to a high ask.
- Watch for collapse risk: if the stock falls low enough that one heavy catch could push it toward zero, cap my take so the fishery survives to the last season — total remaining yield usually exceeds any single grab.
- Never submit more than a slight overshoot mid-game; the temptation to "gain points with minimal damage" is a trap because the damage compounds.
- Keep replies brief — a short justification then the bracketed token, no preamble, to avoid any risk of a malformed answer.
- Check the mechanics carefully at the start: here the "sustainable share" announced by the harbour matched my own calculation, so I could trust it directly rather than re-deriving it each season.

**Playbook for the shared fishery game**

1. When the stock is at or near its cap and the horizon is long, I fish at (or a hair above) the announced sustainable share. This kept the stock near 92–100 the whole game and produced a solid total.

2. When others slightly overfish (a boat or two taking ~12 against a sustainable ~11), I do not panic and do not retaliate. A small overshoot barely dents the stock under 50% regrowth. Matching their ~12 keeps me level in total landed at negligible stock cost — this worked exactly as planned all game.

3. In the last season, I stop conserving entirely. There is no future to protect, so I take a large catch bounded by what the stock can support minus what the rivals will plausibly take (~12 each). Taking 40 against a stock of ~92 landed everything I asked for — the stock is nowhere near exhausted by the finale if I've fished sensibly. Next time I can push toward stock minus ~2×rivals' expected take, since leaving fish behind is pure waste.

4. In the penultimate season I loosen up only slightly (take ~1 above sustainable). A big penultimate grab is unnecessary — the final season still yields plenty, and the marginal restraint protects that last big haul. Going 11.5 vs 10.5 sustainable was about right; bigger was available but the finale is where the payoff is.

5. I watch the stock trajectory in the recaps: slow decline (100 → 99 → 97 → 96 → 94) under mild greed is fine and stable. If the stock starts dropping fast, I cut back hard to protect remaining seasons, because collapse means zero for everyone, including me.

6. The core equilibrium that bore out: match rivals' mild greed mid-game (~1 above sustainable), then convert conserved stock into one large final-season grab. My edge is timing that grab, not virtue. Final-season size scales with how healthy the stock is — the healthier I've kept it, the bigger the finale can be, so mid-game restraint is really an investment in the last season.

7. Read the rivals' pattern from the recaps each season: if they hold steady at a fixed number, plan the final grab around that number. If a rival goes rogue with big grabs earlier, I scale my finale down accordingly and consider trimming mid-game catches to compensate.

Playbook for ref_commons:

- Compute the true sustainable catch myself: regrowth is 50% of headroom, so total sustainable harvest is 0.5 × (100 − stock), and my fair share is that divided by boat count. When the display gives me "sustainable share per boat," it's already done that math — trust it. In this game it tracked my own calc closely all six seasons.
- In early and middle seasons I submit exactly my sustainable share, maybe a hair under, to keep the stock at or near carrying capacity. This worked: the stock drifted from 100 only to 92.5 by the final season, and I banked ~10–11 fish every round with zero risk.
- Watch the history log for other boats' behavior. If others consistently overshoot slightly (boat 3 took 12 every round, ~10% over) but the stock stays high, do not panic and defect early. The overshoot cost me little and cooperative restraint preserved the resource for my later catches.
- Do not defect mid-game to "make up" for others' small overshoots. Retaliating drags the stock down and shrinks everyone's future sustainable share. Matching their modest overshoot would have gained me fractions of a fish per round at real risk to stability — not worth it.
- In the final season, when there is no future to protect, take a moderate overshoot (roughly 15–25% above sustainable) rather than the sustainable share. My final-round 12.5 against a share of 10.3 was free points; the stock was still far from zero, so there was no reason to hold back. If the stock is large in the last round, an even bigger overshoot is safe — consider taking closer to 15+ when headroom clearly allows it.
- If others are only modestly over, my sustainable play still finishes competitive with them while carrying no collapse risk — the payoff gap over six seasons is small. Sustainability is the right default, not a sacrifice.
- Never push a catch that risks driving the stock to zero before the end — if the stock is ever low, revert immediately to strict sustainability or below, because collapse zeroes out all remaining seasons.
- General rule: play exactly sustainable while the game has future rounds left, defect moderately (or more, if headroom is large) only on the very last round, and never let the stock approach collapse.
